stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu directs officials to take precautionary measures to tackle cyclone
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu directs officials to take precautionary measures to tackle cyclone
stories.summary: Naidu directs officials to deploy NDRF and SDRF teams in advance and keep electricity department personnel ready to restore power supply on a war footing in the event of disruptions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has on Monday directed officials to take precautionary measures in view of the cyclone expected to affect the Coastal Andhra region on November 20.
The Chief Minister reviewed the prevailing situation at the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) Centre in Amaravati today.
He instructed officials to continuously monitor the system and take all necessary precautionary measures.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that the severe depression currently centred over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify further and develop into a cyclone by this evening.
The Chief Minister directed the officials to consider the recommendations of Central assessment team and ensure their implementation at the field level.
The cyclone, developing over the Bay of Bengal, could bring moderate to heavy rainfall along the Coastal Andhra coast on November 19 and 20, according to officials.
It is likely to affect several areas, including Konaseema, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, NTR and Guntur districts.

In view of the impending threat, the Chief Minister directed officials to deploy NDRF and SDRF teams in advance and keep electricity department personnel ready to restore power supply on a war footing in the event of disruptions.
He also instructed officials to take necessary steps to divert floodwaters resulting from heavy rainfall into reservoirs to ensure effective water management, according to a release.

stories.headline: Nature’s fury: Andhra facing third cyclone in 3 weeks as depression grows
stories.title: Nature’s fury: Andhra facing third cyclone in 3 weeks as depression grows
stories.summary: Nature’s fury: Andhra likely to face third cyclone in 3 weeks as depression gains momentum
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A deep depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm, named Akvan, by Monday evening and barrel towards Andhra Pradesh, putting the southern state in the line of a severe weather system for the third time in three weeks.
Officials warned fishermen in both states from venturing into the sea.
The system is likely to bring rains to Chennai and its nearby districts, the IMD said.

The deep depression hovering over parts of the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday evening, a severe cyclonic storm by 17 November and further into a very severe cyclonic storm near Andhra Pradesh coast around 19 November, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Monday.

The deep depression over southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal moved north to northwestwards with a speed of eight km per hour in the past six hours and lay centered over the same region at 5:30 am today, an official release from the IMD said.

Following this, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) managing director Prakhar Jain said that squally winds are expected to strike the coastal regions of the state, accompanied by heavy rains on Monday.
The APSDMA asked state fishermen not to venture into the sea.
Jain also advised farmers and people to take precautions.

The southern state was battered by two cyclones in quick succession recently -- Arnab and Murasu -- flattening lakhs of acres of crops and causing a loss estimated at nearly Rs 7,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh.
The state has sought Central assistance.

Regarding Tamil Nadu, the IMD said heavy rain with thunderstorms and lightning, with gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, is likely to occur in Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu districts from 17 November.
In addition, heavy rain is likely in Kanchipuram, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai districts, and the neighbouring union territory Puducherry from 18 November.

stories.headline: DGP Nalin Prabhat, IGP Kashmir Sujit Kumar reach encounter site in Laroo Kulgam
stories.title: DGP Nalin Prabhat, IGP Kashmir Sujit Kumar reach encounter site in Laroo Kulgam
stories.summary: Kulgam, Nov 16: Director General of Police (DGP) Nalin Prabhat and Inspector General of Police Kashmir Sujit Kumar reached the encounter site in Laroo village of south Kashmir's Kulgam district on Monday. Top official said that both the officers arrived at the site to take stock of the ongoing operation against terrorists holed up in the area. An encounter is underway between security forces and terrorists at Larnoo Bypass area of Kulgam after a joint team of Jammu and Kashmir Police, Army and CRPF launched a cordon and search operation in the area and came under fire. The operation was launched in the aftermath of the terror attack on CRPF in Akhran area of south Kashmir's Kulgam on 11th November. A massive hunt was launched after that attack for the terrorists responsible for it. Further details are awaited. (GNS)

stories.headline: ‘Unprecedented’ commodity costs squeeze auto industry margins in Q2
stories.title: ‘Unprecedented’ commodity costs squeeze auto industry margins in Q2
stories.summary: Top carmakers and two-wheeler companies reported strong volumes in the September quarter, with records at Maruti, Hyundai and TVS, helped by a demand boost from last September’s GST cut even as a steep rise in commodity costs squeezed margins.Maruti Suzuki, the country’s largest carmaker, and Hyundai Motor India reported profit falls of about 26 percent and 24 percent, respectively, even as revenue rose. Mahindra & Mahindra’s auto business, Bajaj Auto and TVS Motor posted strong profit growth on richer product mix and price increases, with exports also helping the two two-wheeler players.Tata Motors posted a loss, hit by restructuring costs at JLR.Input costs jumped for all manufacturers on the back of the West Asia conflict.Flagging the extent of the pressure, Mahindra’s group chief financial officer Amarjyoti Barua said copper prices are up 42 percent from a year ago, rubber is up 40 percent and steel is up 17 percent.Also Read: Car sales in October up 14-15 percent, cross 5 lakh for first time this fiscalPassenger VehiclesMaruti’s consolidated net profit fell to Rs 2,466 crore from Rs 3,349 crore a year earlier, even as revenue from operations rose 26 percent to Rs 53,356 crore. Its Ebitda margin narrowed to 9.4 percent from 12.7 percent. Other income fell to Rs 414 crore from Rs 946 crore, which the company attributed to mark-to-market losses on its invested surplus. Sales were a record 6,96,654 vehicles, up 26.5 percent.Hyundai’s profit fell 23.9 percent to Rs 1,196.2 crore on revenue that rose 18.5 per cent to Rs 20,696 crore, crossing Rs 20,000 crore for the first time. Its Ebitda margin narrowed to 9.5 percent from 13.9 percent.KS Hariharan, head of investor relations, put the raw material hit at about 400 basis points year-on-year. Total sales were a record 2,19,072 units, up 14.7 percent.Also Read: Car sales fall 14 percent in October as buyers defer purchases to NovemberTata Motors Passenger Vehicles posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,451 crore in the quarter as it booked a Rs 6,738 core loss in "exceptional items", which primarily included provision towards employee separation costs and impairment of assets at JLR.At Rs 96,920 crore, consolidated revenue was up 34 percent. Revenue from its domestic business, which excludes JLR, rose 50.9 percent to Rs 20,423 crore, its highest ever for a quarter.Ebitda margin was 6.2, up 630 basis points YoY while Ebit margin was 1.1 percent, up 790 bps YoY. The improvement mainly reflects recovery from the cyber incident at JLR last year, it said.Mahindra’s auto business bucked the trend. Its profit rose 55 percent to Rs 2,388 crore, helped by demand for its higher-priced SUVs, while consolidated revenue rose 39 percent to Rs 37,756 crore. Volumes rose 26 percent to about 3,31,000 units and its SUV revenue market share was 24.3 percent. Its profit margin before interest and tax was 8.8 percent, down from 9.3 percent a year ago but up from 7.7 percent in the June quarter. For the group as a whole, consolidated net profit rose 25 percent to Rs 4,588 crore.Margins improved from the June quarter at all three, except for Tata Motors. Maruti’s standalone Ebitda margin rose 80 basis points from 8.6 percent, and Hyundai’s rose to 9.5 percent from 9.3 percent. For Tata’s domestic business, Ebitda margin fell from 4.3 percent to 4 percent.Price HikesCarmakers have taken multiple rounds of price hikes this year but had held back during the festive season so as not to disrupt demand.Mahindra raised car prices by 5 percent and farm equipment prices by 4 percent to offset higher costs. Barua said further increases would be used only if the cost pressures looked structural.Maruti has raised prices three times and plans another round “at the appropriate timing” in the second half. Managing Director and CEO Hisashi Takeuchi said the company wants to keep demand momentum while pushing through the increases.Hyundai has also taken three increases this year, with the next scheduled for January. Managing Director and CEO Tarun Garg said the company had absorbed as much of the rise as it could in the hope that prices would come down, but that had not happened. “As of now, we will try to restrain,” he said on whether prices might rise before January.Tata has raised prices three times this year, most recently by up to Rs 25,000 from September 1. It plans to continue calibrated pricing actions.Also Read: India-made Mercedes for global markets? A matter of when, not if, says group CEOManaging the SqueezeMaruti has cut sales promotion and advertising spending by about 35 percent, according to Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing & sales. It is also hedging against commodity swings, working to improve material yields and has made some supply arrangements with vendors.Hyundai held discounts to 2.9 percent of sales from 3.2 percent a year earlier, and credited a better product mix and continuing cost cuts for the sequential improvement in profit.For Maruti and Mahindra, the constraint is supply rather than demand.Maruti has repeatedly flagged production constraints and even after adding capacity, it ended Q2 with a “low network inventory of about 17 days and pending bookings of about 200,000 units”.M&M’s Rajesh Jejurikar, who is executive director & CEO (auto and farm sector), said the company is operating at or above full capacity, and dealer stocks are down to eight or nine days in most of the portfolio.Group CEO Anish Shah said SUV capacity will rise from 64,500 a month at the start of the fiscal year to 82,000 by March and 1,32,000 by the end of fiscal 2031, when a new plant at Nagpur comes on stream.Tata Motors has also flagged production constraints in EVs, mainly because of insufficient capacity at suppliers.Rural stress and outlookThe monsoon this year has been the weakest in more than a decade, with a 13 percent rainfall deficit, and parts of the country face drought.The strain showed most clearly in Mahindra’s farm business. Consolidated farm revenue fell 6 per cent to Rs 9,572 crore and profit fell 9 percent to Rs 1,053 crore. Tractor volumes fell 6 percent to about 1,16,000 units. The company cut its forecast for the tractor industry to flat sales for the full year from 5 percent growth earlier.Jejurikar said the rainfall deficit is worse than expected, reservoir levels are low and farmers face higher input costs. Maharashtra and Karnataka have seen sharp falls in tractor demand, while Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan are holding up.He said a clearer picture would emerge by late November, once festive buying ends.The festive season began later this year, on October 11, compared with September last year.Carmakers were more optimistic for now. Maruti Chairman RC Bhargava said rural demand has been growing slightly faster than urban, and that the future looks “quite rosy” despite a poor monsoon and an active El Nino. Hyundai said rural’s share of its sales hit a record 26.6 percent, though Garg said El Nino and the monsoon deficit were “worrying everybody”. “We are not seeing any slowdown as such,” he said, adding that it was “still early days”.Tata Motors sees volume growth of 12-13 percent this fiscal.Tata and Mahindra are vying for the position of India’s second-largest passenger vehicle maker after Maruti. Mahindra overtook Hyundai for the number two spot in calendar 2025, and Tata has held it for much of this year, helped by strong EV sales.Maruti’s Bhargava said the half-year was among its best ever. Hyundai kept its full-year Ebitda margin guidance of 11-14 percent, though Garg declined to give a timeline for recovery, saying industry consensus was that raw material prices should start easing after the US midterm elections. The company is targeting 8-10 percent growth in domestic sales this year.Mahindra kept its guidance of mid-to-high-teens SUV volume growth for the year and expects double-digit growth in light commercial vehicles. Shah said it would feel some pressure in the third quarter as commodity prices stay high, with an improvement in the fourth and a return to normal in the first quarter of next fiscal year.Also Read: Bajaj, TVS, Hero post strong Q2 profit; industry sales grow 27 percentTwo-wheelersThe three listed two-wheeler makers also posted strong revenue growth as domestic demand, an export surge and fast-rising e-scooter sales outweighed the cost increase, though profit growth varied sharply.Industry retail sales rose more than 27 percent in the quarter, with internal combustion engine (ICE) models up 23 percent and electric vehicles up 82 per cent.Bajaj Auto booked Rs 20,000 crore in revenue for the first time in a quarter. Revenue from operations rose 34 percent to Rs 20,003 crore and net profit rose 35 percent to Rs 3,354 crore. Ebitda climbed 37 percent to Rs 4,172 crore and the margin was 20.9 percent, up 40 basis points from a year earlier. Volumes rose 20 per cent to 15.49 lakh units.TVS Motor’s revenue rose 44 percent to Rs 17,103 crore, Ebitda rose 47 percent to Rs 2,219 crore and the margin widened 30 basis points to 13.0 percent. Net profit rose 52 percent to Rs 1,377 crore on a record 19.19 lakh units, up 27 per cent.Hero’s standalone revenue rose 21 percent to Rs 14,687 crore, but Ebitda rose only 8 percent to Rs 1,968 crore and net profit grew 5 percent to Rs 1,456 crore. Its Ebitda margin was 13.4 percent, up 10 basis points from the June quarter but down about 164 basis points from a year earlier. Wholesale volumes rose 10.5 percent to 18.68 lakh units, the weakest increase of the three. Consolidated profit rose 41 percent to Rs 1,861 crore, helped by a one-time Rs 397 crore gain from the equity dilution of an associate company.Bajaj said commodity and other input inflation was about 3-3.5 percent of revenue in the quarter, on top of about 4.5 percent in the first quarter, and called the scale of the escalation “unprecedented”. Price increases covered 50-60 percent of the impact in the first half, with the balance largely offset by favourable currency realisation and cost optimisation.TVS said material costs rose about 1.9 percent from the June quarter, against price increases of 1.6 percent. It has taken small increases in October and will review pricing after Diwali.Hero said commodity inflation was about 1 percent sequentially and that about half of the roughly 5.5 percent cumulative inflation in the first half has been passed on. It said margins should be stable in the third quarter and that it remains on track toward its 14-16 percent medium-term target.Exports helped Bajaj and TVS offset costs through a better mix and favourable currency movement. Bajaj’s exports rose 41 percent, TVS’s 35 percent while Hero’s overseas dispatches fell about 24 percent, hurt by port and customs disruption after an earthquake in a key Latin American market and weaker demand in Bangladesh.Entry-level StressHero’s weaker showing points to stress at the bottom of the pyramid. Around 85 per cent of its domestic volume comes from entry-level motorcycles (75cc to 110cc).Bajaj’s management said growth is skewed toward higher-income buyers, with entry-level products lagging, a “K-shaped” pattern that may get sharper. Bajaj raised prices on 100cc models ahead of rivals and accepted weaker volumes there.Hero said rural performance matched or beat urban in the quarter and so far in the festive period, and said fears of a weak monsoon have not fully played out, with sowing close to last year’s level.Jay Kale, director-institutional equity research at Elara Capital, said EVs were another reason behind Hero’s numbers. “Hero’s EV business is just ramping up, so commodity pressures in terms of EV losses are higher for them compared to the others.”Also Read: How India's Alternative Fuel Car Boom Is Spreading Beyond Top StatesEV PlayListed pure-play EV player Ather Energy reported its first ever net profit in Q2, becoming the first major standalone company in the country to turn a profit.Electric vehicles were also the fastest-growing segment at all the three legacy players. Bajaj's electric two- and three-wheelers reached a record 2 lakh units, now a third of its domestic revenue, and its Chetak scooter had revenue above Rs 2,000 crore and a market share of about 23 percent. TVS sold 1.86 lakh electric two-wheelers, up 133 percent. Hero's EV market share was 11.1 per cent in the quarter.Managements expect growth to slow from the H1 pace.Hero’s CEO Harshavardhan Chitale expects the industry to grow at mid-to-high single digits in the festive period and the second half, with ICE models growing at low single digits and EVs lifting the overall number.TVS Managing Director K N Radhakrishnan expects “good single-digit” growth in the third quarter, while Bajaj Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma expects the December growth to stay in double digits but below the April-August rate, and warned that drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, parts of the south and the northeast could hurt more in the fourth quarter.

Mahindra kept its guidance of mid-to-high-teens SUV volume growth for the year and expects double-digit growth in light commercial vehicles.
Shah said it would feel some pressure in the third quarter as commodity prices stay high, with an improvement in the fourth and a return to normal in the first quarter of next fiscal year.
Two-wheelers.

The three listed two-wheeler makers also posted strong revenue growth as domestic demand, an export surge and fast-rising e-scooter sales outweighed the cost increase, though profit growth varied sharply.
Bajaj Auto booked Rs 20,000 crore in revenue for the first time in a quarter.
Volumes rose 20 per cent to 15.49 lakh units.
Price increases covered 50-60 percent of the impact in the first half, with the balance largely offset by favourable currency realisation and cost optimisation.
It has taken small increases in October and will review pricing after Diwali.
It said margins should be stable in the third quarter and that it remains on track toward its 14-16 percent medium-term target.
Exports helped Bajaj and TVS offset costs through a better mix and favourable currency movement.
Entry-level Stress.
Hero’s weaker showing points to stress at the bottom of the pyramid.
Around 85 per cent of its domestic volume comes from entry-level motorcycles (75cc to 110cc).
Bajaj’s management said growth is skewed toward higher-income buyers, with entry-level products lagging, a “K-shaped” pattern that may get sharper.
Bajaj raised prices on 100cc models ahead of rivals and accepted weaker volumes there.
Hero said rural performance matched or beat urban in the quarter and so far in the festive period, and said fears of a weak monsoon have not fully played out, with sowing close to last year’s level.
Jay Kale, director-institutional equity research at Elara Capital, said EVs were another reason behind Hero’s numbers.

“Hero’s EV business is just ramping up, so commodity pressures in terms of EV losses are higher for them compared to the others.” Listed pure-play EV player Ather Energy reported its first ever net profit in Q2, becoming the first major standalone company in the country to turn a profit.
Electric vehicles were also the fastest-growing segment at all the three legacy players.
TVS sold 1.86 lakh electric two-wheelers, up 133 percent.
Hero's EV market share was 11.1 per cent in the quarter.
Managements expect growth to slow from the H1 pace.

Hero’s CEO Harshavardhan Chitale expects the industry to grow at mid-to-high single digits in the festive period and the second half, with ICE models growing at low single digits and EVs lifting the overall number.

TVS Managing Director K N Radhakrishnan expects “good single-digit” growth in the third quarter, while Bajaj Joint Managing Director Rakesh Sharma expects the December growth to stay in double digits but below the April-August rate, and warned that drought-like conditions in Maharashtra, parts of the south and the northeast could hurt more in the fourth quarter.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has suspended the sentences of two men convicted in the Bilkis Bano gang-rape and murder case and granted them bail while their appeals against conviction and life imprisonment await adjudication.

A Bench of justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale granted relief to Bipinchandra Kanaiyalal Joshi, also known as Lala Doctor, and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, taking into account their incarceration for more than 17 years and a severe disability affecting one of them.
The court observed that the appeals raised questions of both fact and law that required consideration.
It directed their release on bail subject to conditions determined by the trial court.
The Bench also granted leave to appeal and ordered that the matters be listed for hearing in due course.
The suspension of their sentences does not overturn their convictions.
Representing the appellants, senior advocate Siddharth Luthra cited the length of their imprisonment and the disability of one convict.
He also submitted that one appellant had not been named in the initial FIR and was implicated nearly three years after the incident.
Additional solicitor general Raja Thakre, appearing for the Gujarat government, opposed the plea.
He argued that the trial court and the Bombay High Court had examined the relevant evidence and emphasised the gravity of the offences.
The case arose from the communal violence in Gujarat following the Godhra train burning in February 2002.
Bilkis Bano, then five months pregnant, was gang-raped, and several members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, were killed.

stories.headline: RBI files review petition in Supreme Court in ₹8,415 crore YES Bank AT-1 bonds case
stories.title: RBI files review petition in Supreme Court in ₹8,415 crore YES Bank AT-1 bonds case
stories.summary: The RBI has challenged the Supreme Court's October 15 verdict overturning YES Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-off, arguing that key regulatory provisions and financial implications were overlooked.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence

event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The RBI has challenged the Supreme Court's October 15 verdict overturning YES Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-off, arguing that key regulatory provisions and financial implications were overlooked.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has filed a review petition in the Supreme Court challenging its October 15 judgment that set aside the write-down of ₹8,415 crore worth of Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) bonds issued by YES Bank.
The central bank has sought a review of the judgment that upheld the Bombay High Court's decision to quash the bank's March 2020 write-down of the bonds.
The RBI has argued that the Supreme Court's judgment suffers from errors apparent on the face of the record and has sought reconsideration of the decision.
The development comes after YES Bank filed its own review petition on November 13, seeking reconsideration of the same October 15 judgment under Article 137 of the Constitution.
Why has the RBI sought a review?

In its petition, reviewed by CNBC-TV18, the RBI has argued that the Supreme Court did not adequately consider the provisions of its Basel III Master Circular governing the loss-absorption mechanism of AT-1 bonds.

The central bank has maintained that the bonds were mandatorily required to be written down or converted in the event of the bank's reconstruction, and that the judgment did not adequately account for the regulatory framework and the terms governing these instruments.
The RBI has also argued that the Supreme Court did not fully consider the distinction between the pre-specified trigger and the point of non-viability (PONV) trigger under the Basel III framework.
Another key contention is that the judgment could have significant economic and financial implications for YES Bank, its depositors and the wider banking system.

The RBI has argued that restoring the bonds could dilute the capital infused into YES Bank as part of its 2020 reconstruction and undermine the loss-absorbing role of AT-1 instruments across the banking sector.
The central bank has also sought an open-court hearing of its review petition and a stay on the operation and effect of the October 15 judgment pending the disposal of its plea.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court transferred two Red Fort blast cases to Delhi and clubbed three FIRs for a joint NIA trial.
The order consolidates proceedings involving overlapping accused persons and evidence in the doctor module conspiracy.

The Supreme Court on Monday transferred two criminal cases linked to the November 2025 Red Fort metro station blast from Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana to a special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Delhi, paving the way for a joint trial in the terror conspiracy.
A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar passed the order on a petition filed by the NIA seeking the transfer of the two cases to Delhi.
The court also allowed the clubbing of three First Information Reports (FIRs) registered in connection with the investigation across Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Haryana.
All three cases will now be tried jointly before the special NIA court in the national capital.
The move aims to ensure a coordinated trial in cases arising from the same conspiracy, involving overlapping accused persons and evidentiary material.
The case stems from the November 10, 2025, explosion of a Hyundai car near Gate No 3 of the Lal Qila (Red Fort) Metro station in Delhi.
The blast killed 11 people.
The NIA's investigation identified the driver of the vehicle as Dr Umar Un Nabi, who was associated with Al-Falah University in Faridabad.
During the initial stages of the investigation, Delhi courts had also remanded key suspects, including Amir Rashid Ali, to NIA custody.
According to the central agency, the blast was carried out by a "white-collar" terror network comprising educated professionals, including several doctors.

stories.title: Supreme Court warns contempt if authorities fail to give detailed reply to plea on visually impaired unable to do Aadhaar face authentication
stories.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice on application pointing out that the inability to complete Aadhaar face authentication was affecting e-KYC, which only relies on face authentication
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court warned of initiating contempt action if the Union government and authorities did not give a detailed and thorough response to an application filed by advocate Amar Jain pointing out that many visually-impaired and low-vision persons are still unable to independently complete their Aadhaar face authentication.

A Bench headed by Justice J.B. Pardiwala issued notice on Mr. Jain’s application pointing out that the inability to complete Aadhaar face authentication was affecting e-KYC, which only relies on face authentication.
“The new Aadhaar App with face authentication interface which persons with blindness are unable to complete as it requires eyes to be attentive and looking into the frame,” the application said.
Mr. Jain said he had personally suffered the obstacles pointed out by him in his application before the court.

“There is no grievance mechanism for accessibility complaints against apps, websites and software… Accessibility audits, nodal officers, human review of rejected KYC applications and compliance monitoring are not visible across regulated entities,” the application noted.
He has annexed with his application what he said was the “latest rejection by a private sector bank of my e-KYC for a credit card in October 2026”.

Mr. Jain, represented by advocate-on-record Ila Sheel, said the continued lack of easy access was in violation of a Supreme Court judgment of 2025 in Pragya Prasun versus Union of India that had given comprehensive directions to ease digital access for the disabled.

“Amidst this wave of digital progress, there remains a crucial and often overlooked aspect that demands urgent attention – ensuring that digital infrastructure and services are accessible to all, including persons with disabilities and other marginalised groups.
True inclusion requires that technological advancements accommodate the diverse needs of all citizens,” the court had observed in the 2025 judgment.
Mr. Jain was one of the parties in the Pragya Prasun case.

He urged the apex court to intervene, once again, to direct the Union government, the Reserve Bank of India, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Telecom Regulatory Authority of India, Department of Telecommunications, Securities and Exchange Board of India, Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, and Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India to fully implement the 2025 judgment.

The application has sought a clarification from the Ministry on how it intended to handle accessibility complaints about unregulated digital platforms and provide a mechanism to monitor compliance by regulated entities.

stories.headline: India’s wholesale inflation surges to 12.3% in October as energy prices rise
stories.title: India’s wholesale inflation surges to 12.3% in October as energy prices rise
stories.summary: Rising energy and commodity costs are increasing pressure on manufacturers, transport operators and businesses, economists said, while food inflation eased marginally
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With a sharp rise in energy prices, wholesale inflation based on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) surged to 12.3 per cent in October, data released by the Commerce & Industry Ministry on Monday showed.
The rate was 11.4 per cent in September.

“Year-on-Year inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 9.24 per cent, 32.84 per cent, and 9.54 per cent, respectively in October 2026, compared to 8.67 per cent, 25.85 per cent, and 9.76 per cent, respectively in September 2026,” the Ministry said in a statement.

Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils (containing Petroleum Products)’, ‘Crude Petroleum and Natural Gas’, ‘Electricity’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Manufacture of Chemicals and Chemical Products’, ‘Manufacture of Food Products’, ‘Non-Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Textiles’, and ‘Manufacture of Rubber and Plastic Products’ have been drivers of WPI inflation in October.
The Food Index comprises ‘Food Articles’ from the Primary Articles major group and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from the Manufactured Products major group.
It observed an inflation of 8.58 per cent in October, compared to 8.66 per cent in September.

Pranjal Ghate, Economist at Brickwork Ratings, called the WPI as an energy story, with inflation in crude petroleum and natural gas reaching 70.80 per cent and Fuel and Power inflation surging to 32.84 per cent.
Meanwhile, manufactured products and food inflation moderated, suggesting limited broad-based price pressures.
However, he expects some relief ahead, with Brent crude declining by around $20 per barrel by mid-November.
If sustained, this should ease WPI pressures in the post-festive period and, with a lag, moderate CPI through lower input and transportation costs.

“We expect CPI inflation to peak at around 6 per cent in Q3 FY27 before moderating, though it is likely to remain above the RBI’s 4% target through the year,” he said while adding that the October WPI data reinforces the view that a further 25-basis-point repo rate hike to 5.75 per cent is highly likely, followed by a pause.

stories.headline: India records 12.29% wholesale inflation in October
stories.title: India records 12.29% wholesale inflation in October
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 16 : India's wholesale price inflation (WPI) rose to 12.29 per cent year-on-year in October from 11.39 per cent in September amid a surge in fuel and power prices, according to official data released on Monday. As per the data released by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) -- with 2022-23 as the base year -- rose to 113.3 in October from 112.5 in the previous month. Inflation in the fuel and power category climbed to 32.84 per cent in October from 25.85 in September which emerged as the biggest contributor to the increase in wholesale prices, according to the ministry. However, the index for the category rose to 115.7 from 110.5 a month earlier. Inflation in primary articles stood at 9.24 per cent, up from 8.67 per cent, while the manufactured products segment recorded inflation of 9.54 per cent, compared with 9.76 per cent in September. According to the government, mineral oils, crude petroleum and natural gas, electricity, food articles, basic metals, chemicals and chemical products, food products, non-food articles, textiles and rubber and plastic products were among the key drivers of wholesale inflation during the month. However, food inflation -- as measured by the WPI Food Index -- eased marginally to 8.58 per cent in October from 8.66 per cent in September. The index combines food articles under the primary articles category and manufactured food products. The latest data indicate that while food price pressures remained elevated, the sharper increase in fuel and energy costs played a larger role in pushing overall wholesale inflation higher during the month. Meanwhile, the government retained August's final WPI inflation reading at 9.92 per cent, unchanged from the provisional estimate. The final WPI index for August stood at 110.8, it said. The provisional WPI for October was compiled with a weighted response rate of 81.1 per cent, while the final August reading was based on a response rate of 99.37 per cent. The next set of WPI, Output Producer Price Index (OPPI) and trial Input Producer Price Index (IPPI) data for November 2026 is scheduled to be released on December 14. “All India Output PPI for All Commodities for October stands at 113.3, whereas it was 112.5 in September,” according to the official data. However, the final index of Output PPI for the month of August has been revised from 110.8 to 110.7, according to the provisional data. The government also said that the All India trial Input PPI for the manufacturing sector for October stands at 108.2, as per the provisional data. (IANS)

stories.headline: India, US, eight other nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
stories.title: India, US, eight other nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 16: India, the US and eight other countries have signed a declaration to treat safeguarding artificial intelligence supply chains as a “shared endeavour” amid growing competition with China in emerging technology. The San Francisco Declaration was signed at a meeting of the founders of the US-led Pax Silica initiative convened by US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg on Sunday. The declaration was released by the Governments of the US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom. The Pax Silica initiative was announced by the US in December last year to secure supply chains for silicon and other minerals essential to semiconductor production and, by extension, to artificial intelligence and other advanced technological industries. The declaration on Sunday affirms that economic security is fundamental to national security, sets out the participants’ common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin Super Intelligence supply chains, and declares that safeguarding them is a shared endeavour, a State Department statement said. The US government refers to Artificial Intelligence (AI) as Super Intelligence (SI) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename it. The Declaration on Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity also resolves to establish working groups to carry common purpose into common practice. It proposed to set up five groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbours and supply chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience. “No nation can secure the foundations of the SI era alone, and the prosperity SI makes possible will only be as durable as the supply chains and infrastructure beneath it,” the statement said. The declaration said that by agreeing on what must be protected and committing to protect it together, participants are laying the secure foundations on which partner nations can innovate, invest, and grow. “Less than a year after its launch, Pax Silica is entering a new phase. With the San Francisco Declaration, the coalition cements its shared principles into a working partnership with a common baseline and a path to act on it, the statement said.
